subject: Application Design (Twelve-Factor)

findings.subject: Application Design
findings.title: Environment-specific backing-service config is hardcoded in versioned appsettings files instead of environment variables
findings.recommendation: Remove real/placeholder host, port, username and password values from appsettings*.json (checked into source control). Bind only structural defaults from JSON and supply the actual per-deploy values (DataSources:*:Host/Port/UserName/Password) via environment variables, dotnet user-secrets in dev, or a secret store (e.g. Azure Key Vault) in higher environments — ASP.NET Core's built-in environment-variable configuration provider already overrides these keys, so only the committed literal values need to move out.

findings.subject: Application Design
findings.title: Serilog File sink manages log rotation/retention itself instead of treating logs as an event stream
findings.recommendation: Write logs only to stdout (the existing Console sink) and let the execution environment (container runtime, systemd, or a log-shipping agent) handle routing, rotation, and retention, rather than having the app manage rolling files and retention counts itself.

strengths.subject: Application Design
strengths.title: Single solution/repo tracks the whole app across all layers

evidence.excerpt: PilotUtilityApi.Shared / Domain / Repositories / Services / Web projects all in one solution

strengths.subject: Application Design
strengths.title: Dependencies explicitly declared with centrally pinned exact versions

strengths.subject: Application Design
strengths.title: Backing data sources are attached as swappable config-bound resources, not hardwired in code

checkResults.subject: Application Design
checkResults.reason: Host, port, username and password fields for both data sources are literal values committed in appsettings.json/appsettings.Development.json rather than sourced from environment variables.

checkResults.subject: Application Design
checkResults.reason: The .NET SDK inherently separates build (dotnet build/publish, producing versioned artifacts), release (config-bound at startup via appsettings/env), and run (dotnet exec/Kestrel Run()) stages; CI/CD pipeline specifics are covered under the Software Lifecycle subject, not reviewed here.

checkResults.subject: Application Design
checkResults.reason: No in-process state or anti-patterns blocking horizontal scale-out were found in the files reviewed; ASP.NET Core's process/request model scales via additional process instances.

checkResults.subject: Application Design
checkResults.reason: Serilog is configured with a File sink that performs rolling-interval and retention-count log management in addition to Console output.

checkResults.subject: Application Design
checkResults.reason: No one-off admin/migration process scripts or tooling are present among the files in scope for this batch.

notes: No Dockerfile/docker-compose/.env.example exist in the repo (confirmed absent by the orchestrator), so containerization-specific evidence for TF-07/TF-10 was not available; conclusions rely on ASP.NET Core/Kestrel framework defaults instead. CI/CD pipeline files were out of scope for this batch, so TF-05 was assessed from the .NET build/publish/run model rather than pipeline evidence.
